objective: Census every symmetric law of bits on the edges of a triangulation (a rule on the numbers of 1-edges in each triangle and a rule on the edge-labelling classes of each tetrahedron) against the local identities of the 2-3 and 1-4 moves; certify every failing law on explicit move sequences of singular triangulations of the sphere and two lens spaces; prove that the surviving laws are trivial or parity and that parity counts the mod-2 first cohomology times two to the vertices minus one; show that native networks (bits on faces, shared by exactly two tetrahedra) see only the dual graph, with one-tetrahedron triangulations of the sphere and of L(4,1) that share their native network.
status: Proved by HUB-DIMENSION-20261024-001A-P001 (V1 prose proof with standard-library check; move connectivity cited). Of 32,768 symmetric edge laws, those passing the 2-3 and 1-4 identities reduce to seven: four trivial laws and three parity laws, whose normalized counts are constants or |H^1(M; Z/2)|; every other ever-allowed law breaks on sampled moves. Native networks see only the dual graph (the sphere and L(4,1) share one, while edge parity counts 1 and 2). Bits see dimension three only through hubs, and then only through mod-2 first cohomology.
title: Bits see a three-manifold only through its mod-2 cohomology
